subject: research/holdout-market
professional: a referee for a mechanism-design / learning-theory venue (EC, COLT, or the adaptive-data-analysis track at NeurIPS) who knows the Ladder, the reusable holdout and Abernethy-Frongillo markets; first checks: do the tables reproduce, is each stated result actually true in general or only on the tested instance, is the attack the strongest known one (Blum-Hardt's boosting attack), does the Ladder guarantee mean anything at n=100, and is the nearest prior work (Harris and Waggoner's holdout-paid blockchain markets, Blum-Hardt's own attack) cited and compared

evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` (29 s) and diffed it with experiments/results.txt: identical, all three tables. Independent re-implementation in scratchpad hm_indep.py (numpy vectorised clipped log loss, own SGD, own market and ladder logic; only the RNG call order is shared so the same worlds are drawn): raw k=100 paid 0.0670 / true -0.0366 / over 0.1036 / accepted 26.6; raw k=5000 0.1475 / -0.3707 / 0.5182 / 232.6; ladder eta=0.02 k=5000 0.0075 / -0.0016 / 0.0091 / 0.4; honest phase ladder eta=0.10 paid 0.313 true 0.280: all equal to results.txt to the printed digit. Per-seed spread (not reported by the project): the raw k=5000 overpayment is positive on all 8 seeds (min 0.103, sd 0.273), so the headline is robust to seed. Hand checks: theta0 = 0 gives holdout loss exactly ln 2 = 0.6931 whatever the data, so ladder pub0 = round(0.6931/eta)*eta = 0.70 for eta 0.02/0.05/0.10 (observed pub0 0.7000); paper's derived figures 0.148+0.371 = 0.52 overpayment and 0.008/0.002 at eta=0.02 check; '~25%' paid-gain loss at eta=0.1 is 1-0.313/0.408 = 23.3% (true gain 22.7%), acceptable rounding. The numbers are right. One stated result is not: 'splitting changes the total by at most one rung' (whitepaper.md:24-25) is false in general (scratchpad hm_split.py: seed 5, d=5, an overshooting update t1 with holdout loss 0.684 is unpaid as one submission, but split into 40 steps along the same line it is paid 0.26 = 13 rungs, because an intermediate point reaches loss 0.43). On 2,000 instances with a monotone path the gap never exceeded one rung, so the claim holds only on that special case. Scored 3 for the computed outputs; the false general result is charged to claims.
evidence.completeness: Everything the README lists runs: 4 tests pass (1.66 s), run.py reproduces results.txt byte for byte in ~29 s (README says ~35 s), figure.py exists and draws from results.txt. The paper's four results each have a table or a test behind them. Not done and said not done: scaling of eta with n, Thresholdout, fresh-holdout rotation, sybils, stronger attacks. The live page https://marisstella.app/research/holdout-market/ could not be loaded (curl returned 000 through the proxy) and served-copy.mjs reports it is not a published product directory; the homepage summary in research/_homepage/projects.json matches the README.
evidence.verification: `cd research/holdout-market && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 4 tests OK in 1.66 s. Six mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, 1 caught, 5 survived: deleting the ladder's eta gate entirely (market.py:78, `gate = 0.0`), the core of the proposed fix, leaves every test green; so do floor instead of round in the ladder (market.py:72), `<=` instead of `<` in acceptance (market.py:79), widening the probability clip from 1e-3 to 0.05 (market.py:22), and flipping the sign of true gain in run.py:45 (the headline's 'model got worse'). Only paying the unrounded loss (market.py:81) is caught, by the telescoping test. No test pins any number in results.txt, and the splitting and hill-climb tests check one instance each with loose bounds.
evidence.craft: Read src/holdout_market/market.py (98 lines), __init__.py, tests/test_market.py, experiments/run.py, paper/whitepaper.md. Small, stdlib-only, readable, deterministic seeds, numerically stable sigmoid. Defects: the ladder rounds the starting loss (market.py:65), so the honest phase in ladder mode pays up to eta/2 of pure rounding (0.0069 here) before anyone improves anything; experiments are a top-level script with no functions to test; mode='raw' silently ignores eta; budget_bound's docstring relies on loss >= 0 but the bound is stated in terms of the rounded pub0, which can exceed the true starting loss.
evidence.claims: Backed: every number in README.md:13-14 and the paper's results 3 and 4 (recomputed above); '4 tests'; 'payouts telescope to a known budget' (algebraic, tested); 'copying pays nothing' (tested); 'Stylised' and a candid limitations section; the homepage summary. Not backed: (1) 'splitting changes the total by at most one rung (B.eta, tested)' (whitepaper.md:24-25) is false in general, counterexample above, and the test (tests/test_market.py:29) checks one monotone instance; (2) 'the ladder bound is worst-case' (whitepaper.md:48), offered as reassurance against stronger attacks, is vacuous at this scale: Blum-Hardt's leaderboard error bound O((log(kn)/n)^(1/3)) is 0.51 for k=5000, n=100 on a [0,1] loss, times a loss range of ln(1000) = 6.9 here, i.e. larger than the whole signal; (3) '(proved, tested)' for telescoping, but no proof is in the files (it is a one-line argument, so low); (4) homepage 'a Ladder-style threshold removes the attack' is shown only against the weak random-search attacker, not the boosting attack the Ladder paper itself uses.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher designing payments for a decentralised training network wants to know how fast exact holdout-score payments leak and what a ladder costs, and to build on the code. They get a small reproducible simulator and a clear qualitative demonstration. They cannot build a paper on it: one synthetic logistic world, one holdout size, one weak attacker (sigma=0.05 random search), 8 seeds with no intervals, no eta-vs-n scaling, no Thresholdout or fresh-holdout baseline. Nearest prior work (cited from memory, not re-checked here): Blum and Hardt 2015 (ICML) already show a data-less 'boosting attack' against exact leaderboards and the Ladder fix; Hardt 2017 'Climbing a shaky ladder' improves the bounds; Whitehill 2016/2018 attacks AUC oracles; Roelofs et al. 2019 (NeurIPS) measure adaptive overfitting on real Kaggle holdouts; Harris and Waggoner 2019 (IEEE Blockchain, 'Decentralized and collaborative AI on blockchain') deploy exactly an Abernethy-Frongillo-style market paying holdout-loss improvements. The paper honestly frames itself as an adaptation whose contribution is measurement, but omits the boosting attack and Harris-Waggoner, the two closest pieces, so the measurement is of a weaker attack than one already in the literature, in a setting already proposed. Novelty is small.
evidence.domain: Against adaptive-data-analysis practice (Dwork et al. 2015; Blum-Hardt 2015): the raw rule's failure and the ladder are standard and correctly implemented (accept iff loss < published - eta, publish rounded loss), and treating the holdout as consumable is the right lesson. Departures a referee would raise: the attacker is not the known worst case (boosting attack or label-inference), so 'ladder pays ~0' is a statement about random search; eta in [0.02, 0.05] is chosen by eye at n=100, with the n^(-1/3) scaling (0.215 at n=100, before multiplying by the loss range) asserted but not tested; no confidence intervals on 8 seeds; positive-only payments. Below the PhD bar in research/CLAUDE.md: a one-session working note, not a programme step aimed at a venue.

defects.what: Result 2 'under the ladder, splitting changes the total by at most one rung (B.eta, tested)' is false in general: an overshooting update unpaid as one submission (holdout loss 0.684) is paid 0.26 = 13 rungs when split into 40 steps along the same line. It holds only when holdout loss is monotone along the path; the test checks one such instance.

The ladder's eta gate, the core of the proposed fix, is untested: setting gate = 0.0 leaves all 4 tests green, as do floor-vs-round, < vs <=, a 50x wider probability clip, and a sign flip of the headline's true-gain in run.py. 5 of 6 mutants survive; no test pins results.txt.

Nearest prior work missing: Blum and Hardt's own boosting attack (a stronger data-less attacker than the random search used here, in the paper already cited) and Harris and Waggoner 2019 (an Abernethy-Frongillo market paying holdout-loss decreases on a blockchain, the same setting). The 'ladder pays ~0' result is measured only against the weak attacker.
'the ladder bound is worst-case' is offered as reassurance, but the Blum-Hardt bound at k=5000, n=100 is about 0.51 of the loss range (6.9 nats here), vacuous at this scale.
Ladder rounds the starting loss (ln 2 -> 0.70), so the first accepted submission is paid up to eta/2 of rounding that no one earned, and the stated budget bound B*pub0 can exceed B*loss0.
8 seeds with means only: no standard deviations or intervals in results.txt (raw k=5000 overpayment sd is 0.27 on a mean of 0.52); one holdout size; eta-vs-n scaling asserted, not tested.

verdict: A tidy, honest working note whose numbers are right: run.py reproduces results.txt byte for byte and an independent numpy re-implementation reproduces every checked row (raw 5000-query attack paid 0.1475 while true loss worsens 0.3707, overpayment positive on all 8 seeds; ladder pays ~0). It does not meet the bar. Verification is 1: deleting the ladder's eta gate, the mechanism the paper proposes, leaves all four tests green, and 5 of 6 mutants survive. Claims is 2: result 2 ('splitting changes payment by at most one rung') is false in general (a counterexample pays 13 rungs), and the 'worst-case ladder bound' is vacuous at n=100. As research it is a toy demonstration of a known failure (Blum-Hardt's boosting attack is stronger and already in the cited paper; Harris and Waggoner 2019 proposed the same holdout-paid market) with one weak attacker, one holdout size and no intervals, well short of the PhD bar.
